chapters.title: The rise of GCA
chapters.content:
GCA — Ghost Consultant Agency

"Huldra... is pregnant!!!"That was how GCA began.After the verdict of the Dokkaebi and Huldrawas broadcast live on GBS,ghosts from all over the countrystarted coming to me with their problems.




Some ghosts

had disputes with afterlife bureaucrats,

some
caused trouble in the human world,

and some
just did something stupid.

Simple cases
were handled by Agent M.

But sometimes,
the problems involved multiple worlds,
and I had to make the judgment myself.

So people
started calling this work:

GCA — Ghost Consultant Agency.

And
the beginning of all these cases
was this very trial.

Previous Case

Dokkaebi & Huldra

One day, Messenger and Agent M burst into my house—
faces red, hair disheveled, breathing like they had outrun a storm.

Messenger:
"Sir!! I have... a report!!"

Me:
"...What now."

Messenger:

"Huldra... is pregnant!!!"

Me:

"Good. And?"

Agent M:
"The GIA guy came again. He wants to see you."

I put my cup down.

Me:
"Messenger, prepare a live broadcast through GBS—Ghost Broadcasting System.
In one hour. Inform Odin and Yeomra.

Agent M, bring the GIA agent to witness my judgment.
And summon Huldra and the Dokkaebi.

Now."

The couple:
"Y-yes, sir!!!"



One Hour Later — The Trial Begins

Huldra and the Dokkaebi knelt before me
like two drenched puppies.

Me:
"First of all—

Odin and King Yeomra are watching this.
Live.
On TV.

All ghosts from both realms as well.

Isn't that wonderful?"

Me:
"Too much?

You broke my TV.
And my rules.

That earns you a direct ticket
to the Fire-Burning Abyss.

Huldra—tell me.
Who is the father?"

Huldra:
"...The Dokkaebi... sir."

Me:
"Dokkaebi!
Why did she name you as the father?"

Dokkaebi:
"I—I don't know, sir...
But maybe... I have one clue.

I... watched TV...
in her room sometimes..."

Me:
"Strange.
I gave each of you your own television.

Why were you watching in her room?"

Dokkaebi:
"I only taught her how to cook ramyeon!
And we shared kimchi... sir..."

Me:
"Huldra—is that true?"

Huldra:
"Yes, sir... completely true."

Me:
"Ramyeon and kimchi...

Humanism?

No—Ghostism."

Huldra:
"Sir... it was delicious..."

Dokkaebi:
"Best ramyeon in all nine realms, sir..."

Me:
"And soju?"

Huldra:
"...Drinking alone is lonely...
So I asked him to join..."

Me:
"...Fair.
Soju does require another soul."

Ramyeon Cross-Examination

Me:
"Now answer—ON THREE.

'Ramyeon and kimchi are delicious and yummy.'

Three!"

The couple:
"Yes, sir!! Delicious and yummy!!"

Me:
"Good.

Ramyeon and kimchi—
is that Humanism?

Three!"

The couple:
"Of course, sir!"

Me:
"Ramyeon + kimchi + soju = friendship?"

The couple:
"Absolutely, sir!"

Me:
"Very good.

A man and a woman cannot be 'just friends.'

Three."

The couple:
"No doubt, sir!!"

Me:
"And if it goes beyond friendship...
that is love."

The couple:
"Right, sir!"

Me:
"And love... can create a child.

Three... two..."

The couple (defeated):
"...Right, sir......"

THE FINAL VERDICT

Me:
"When in Rome, do as the Romans do.

When in Korea—

you marry,
raise your children,
and serve kimchi properly.

Three!
Two!
One!"

The couple:
"!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!"


Me:
"Odin and Yeomra just called.
Both kings bless your marriage.

Agent M—prepare their honeymoon suite.
...and bring some ginseng for her.

Huldra needs strength—
love consumes a lot of energy."

Agent M:
"Yes, sir. Premium grade.
Six-year root.
Twice steamed."

Dokkaebi (raising his hand timidly):
"Sir... can I have one too...?"

Me:
"No.

You've already used your strength."

I waved my hand toward the darkness—
toward Odin's realm, toward the underworld,
toward every ghost watching on GBS.

Me:
"Live well.

And you—GIA agent.
Report this verdict to your boss.

Done."

chapters.title: Case 1 - The Legend of A-rang
chapters.content:
After the ghosts' Autumn Sports Day ended,
and a surprising number of spirits voluntarily confessed their past sins,
the Underworld finally settled into peace.

For about three days.

Then Agent M burst into my office.

His face was white.
Not pale.
White.

Agent M:
"General! We have a serious problem!"

Me:
"What kind of problem?"

Agent M:
"Something... even ghosts are afraid of."

Me:
"Ghosts are afraid? What happened? Did the King of the Underworld skip breakfast again?"

Agent M:
"No, sir! You really need to see this one yourself."

Me:
"What is it?"

Agent M:
"A ghost."

Me:
"...We get those a lot."

Agent M:
"But this one... even the Grim Reaper ran away."

Now that got my attention.

Me:
"Bring it in."

Agent M came back with a ghost whose head was covered by a cover,

Agent M:
"Please... don't panic."

He pulled the cloth off.
I tried not to show it, but I almost jumped.

Me:
"...A-rang?"

A-rang:
"Yes, General."

Me:
"Wait. Didn't your story already end? You resolved your grudge and went to the afterlife. Legend complete. Roll credits."

A-rang:
"That was the plan."

Me:
"So what happened?"

A-rang:
"On the way to the Underworld... the Grim Reaper looked at me, screamed, and ran away."

Me:
"...Excuse me?"

A-rang:
"So I couldn't get to the Underworld."

Me:
"...Fair enough."

A-rang:
"I heard rumors among the ghosts that you help them resolve their grudges... and even run rehabilitation programs."

Me:
"...Who keeps leaking my policies?"

A-rang:
"So I walked here from Miryang."

Me:
"That's a two-month trip."

A-rang:
"Yes... but whenever I got near other ghosts, they ran away. So it took me two years."

I stared at her for a moment.

Then I asked:

Me:
"A-rang... have you looked in a mirror lately?"

A-rang:
"No. I've never owned one."

Me:
"Agent M. Mirror."

A full-length mirror arrived shortly after.

Me:
"Alright, A-rang. Take a look."

She stepped toward the mirror.
Slowly.
Very slowly.

She looked.

Three seconds passed.

Then—

A-rang:
"AAAAAAAAAAAH!"

She fainted.

I sighed.

Me:
"This is the first time in history a ghost has fainted from seeing its own face."

I turned to Agent M.

Me:
"This is why ghosts need cultural education programs. And maybe grooming classes."

Eventually, A-rang woke up.

Me:
"Okay. First things first. Let's remove the knife stuck in your neck."

A-rang:
"Oh... that?"

Me:
"Yes. That."

A-rang:
"Is it really that bad?"

Me:
"You have a thirty-stitch scar across your throat. Even Grim Reapers are afraid of you."

I leaned back in my chair.

Me:
"Don't you want to make friends? Maybe date someone?"

A-rang:
"...Date?"

Me:
"Step one: surgery. Step two: recovery. Step three: ten years of volunteer work helping injured ghosts."

She nodded immediately.

A-rang:
"I'll do it! Ten years? I'd do a hundred!"

Me:
"Agent M. Call NGGH."

Agent M:
"The National Ghost General Hospital?"

Me:
"Yes. Knife removal. Scar treatment. Full recovery package."

Then I added:

Me:
"And after that... take her to the bathhouse."

Six months later, a beautiful woman walked into my office.

Me:
"...And you are?"

She smiled.

A-rang:
"It's me! A-rang!"

Me:
"...Modern medicine really is amazing."

A-rang:
"Knife removed! Scars gone! Isn't the world wonderful?"

Me:
"Careful. Now that you're pretty, the Grim Reapers might come back."

A-rang:
"So what's my job?"

Me:
"You know that young ghost who lost his leg?"

A-rang:
"Yes."

Me:
"We bought him a prosthetic leg and crutches. But he refuses rehabilitation."

She cracked her knuckles.

A-rang:
"Oh, that's easy."

Me:
"How?"

She grinned.

A-rang:
"The beauty strategy."

And she ran out the door.

Agent M looked at me.

Agent M:
"Was A-rang always this... energetic?"

Me:
"No idea."

I shrugged.

Me:
"But ghosts who've suffered a lot usually understand each other."

Agent M nodded.

Agent M:
"I never imagined the Legend of A-rang would end like this."

Me:
"Neither did I."

I paused.

A year later, word reached us that A-rang and the young ghost had married
and launched a cosmetics business, "Olive A-rang,"
with the slogan:

"Makeup can deceive even ghosts."

And that... is the modern ending of the Legend of A-rang.

Epilogue

One day, A-rang watched a ghost crawling out of a tablet and made a comment.

A-rang:
"Hey... unnie.
That's not how you do it anymore."

Sadako:
"...What?"

A-rang:
"You come out slowly... long hair... crawling..."
"...no one watches that now."

"If you want views, start with makeup."

"And also... your lighting is terrible."

chapters.title: Case 2 - The Nine-Tailed Fox
chapters.content:
One day, Agent M burst into my office, clearly furious, dragging a fox behind her.
I wondered why she was so emotional.

Me:
"Agent M. What's going on?"

Agent M:
"This shameless creature tried to flirt with my husband, so I arrested her!"

I looked at the fox.

Me:
"...Agent M."

Agent M:
"Yes, sir."

Me:
"Your husband doesn't even have a liver."

A brief silence.

Fox:
"I wasn't flirting! I was asking where the GCA office was, and she dragged me here!

"Why are you looking for GCA?"

Fox:
"I want to become human.
So I've been stealing and eating human livers...
But these days, human men are stronger than me.
Their houses are sturdier, too.
There's nothing I can catch anymore."

Me:
"Why do you want to become human?"

Fox:
"I want to live like humans.
Work. Eat. Sleep.
Not just survive."

Me:
"Then why not a cow?"

Fox:
"Cows are too strong!
If one charges at you, you're seriously injured.
Last time, I broke my ribs.
I almost died."

Me:
"If you became human, could you work?"

Fox:
"If I can eat cow liver, I can work twelve hours a day!"

Me:
"...Alright."

Me:
"What if you could eat as much liver as you wanted in another country?"

Fox:
"Borders don't mean anything to us.
If there's prey, we go."

Me:
"Are you serious?"

Fox:
"I'm truly serious!"

Me:
"...Australia."

A brief silence.

Fox:
"...Australia?"

Me:
"They process hundreds of cows a day.
And Australians usually throw away the liver.
Minimum wage is about twenty dollars an hour.
You'd earn money, get free liver,
and there are millions of rabbits.
They even struggle with rabbit overpopulation."

Fox:
"...A place like heaven exists?"

A brief silence.

Me:
"The work is hard.
The nights are long.
That's why humans avoid it."

Me:
"But for you... it sounds perfect."

Fox:
"Please send me there!"

Me:
"If you go, you live as a human.
No hunting humans."

Fox:
"...Understood."

Me:
"Agent M."

Agent M:
"Yes, sir."

Me:
"Call the Australian Ghost Immigration Office.
Work visa.
Rabbit Control Specialist."

Agent M:
"I'll arrange it immediately."

Me:
"When you get there—work hard. Live well."

Fox:
"Yes, General.
I'll repay this kindness... with the finest liver you'll ever taste."

Epilogue

After she left, the fox donated her entire weekly paycheck to GCA.
She said she didn't need money.

Years later, the fox finally became human.

According to the story,
she became the most popular instagram influencer
after appearing on MasterChef with a cow-liver dish.

chapters.title: Case 3 - Bulgasal
chapters.content:
One day, the local ghosts rushed in, panicking.

A Bulgasal had gone on a rampage in the neighboring village
and was heading toward ours.

Agent M:
"Sir! Is there any way to stop it?"

Me:
"You know there's no simple way.
It eats metal, can't be killed, and you can't reason with it."

Agent M:
"Then what do we do?"

Me:
"Gather the ghosts.
Dig a pit the size of a swimming pool and fill it with oil."

Agent M:
"You're going to burn it?"

Me:
"It won't die.
But if it falls in, it'll be too slippery to climb out. That's enough.
Scatter some metal tools around it.
It'll get distracted eating and fall in."

The next day, we went to check.
The Bulgasal had fallen into the pit
and had been struggling all night.

Me:
"Heeey!!! Long time no see!"

Bulgasal:
"General!!! Please pull me out!"

Me:
"That's not the problem.
You go berserk whenever you see metal.
I was thinking of sealing you in concrete."

Bulgasal:
"That's not fair!
I don't even know why I was created like this!"

Me:
"Created?"

Bulgasal:
"A monk made me out of resentment.
If anyone's responsible, it's him—not me."

A brief silence.

Me:
"...Fair enough."

Me:
"You eat iron and metal, right?
What about ceramics?"

Bulgasal:
"I once ate a computer.
Those blue parts inside? Crunchy. Better than metal."

Me:
"You can survive without air? Even in fire?"

Bulgasal:
"My name literally means I don't die.
Water, fire, air—I don't need any of them."

A brief silence.

Me:
"...Space."

Me:
"Agent M."

Agent M:
"Yes, sir."

Me:
"Send a recommendation to NASA and SpaceX."

Agent M:
"...NASA, sir?"

Me:
"Immortal.
Consumes derelict spacecraft and satellites in orbit."

Two months later, Bulgasal was sent into space
as a specialist in cleaning up decommissioned spacecraft and satellites.

According to legend,
Bulgasal later received a Special Achievement Award from NASA—
and was granted unlimited access to spacecraft.

chapters.title: Case 4 - Evil Spirit
chapters.content:
One day, a ghost dressed like a high school girl walked into my office,

chewing gum, acting like she owned the place.

Evil Spirit:
"Hey, mister.
I heard you grant ghosts' wishes.
What about mine?"

I frowned.

Me:
"...What's your problem?"

Evil Spirit:
"Everything."

Me:
"...For example?"

Evil Spirit:
"...I want a Hermès bag."

A brief silence.

Agent M:
"...Hermès?"

Evil Spirit:
"Yes."

Me:
"Then work at a Hermès factory.
You'll see them every day."

Evil Spirit:
"...Really?"

Me:
"The work is hard."

Evil Spirit:
"That's fine."

Me:
"There's no salary."

A brief silence.

Evil Spirit:
"...As long as I can touch Hermès."

I thought for a moment.

Me:
"...Good."

Agent M:
"...Good?"

Me:
"Work for a hundred years,
you might become a chief designer."

Her eyes lit up.

Me:
"And I'll follow you on Instagram."

Evil Spirit:
"...Why?"

Me:
"You want attention, don't you?"

A brief silence.

Me:
"Post a selfie with a Hermès bag."

Agent M:
"...A selfie?"

Me:
"You'll hit ten million followers in no time."

Me:
"Agent M."

Agent M:
"Yes, sir."

Me:
"Contact the Hermès internship center."

Epilogue

After she left—

Agent M:
"Do you think this will actually work?"

I shook my head.

Me:
"Maybe.

That's a craving for attention and affection...
and also an expression of anxiety about the future."


I paused.

Me:
"If she learns to stitch,
one thread at a time...
she might calm down."


Years later, the evil spirit became a luxury appraiser.

And according to legend,

she finally stopped being angry.

Because—

She had made enough of them.

chapters.title: Case 5 - Jangsanbeom
chapters.content:
One day, Jangsanbeom came to see me.

These days, people watch TV and live in apartments,
so they no longer fall for his tricks or listen to his voice.

He complained that he was starving to death.

Me:
"Jangsanbeom."

Jangsanbeom:
"...Yes."

Me:
"You can perfectly mimic human voices, right?"

Jangsanbeom:
"Yes."

I paused for a moment.

Me:
"Then I guess you can do English too?"

Jangsanbeom:
"...I have lived through wars in this land.
In the Goryeo era, I mastered Mongolian.
In the Joseon era, Manchu, Chinese, and Japanese.
And during the Korean War... English as well."

Me:
"Wow~ You're a linguistic genius!!"

Jangsanbeom:
"I can also replicate any voice perfectly after hearing it once.
Like Jim Carrey~~"


Me:

"If you go to the U.S., you can't eat people there.
Beef is their staple food...
Will you be okay?"

Jangsanbeom:
"I only ate people because there was no beef... hehe.
If beef is the staple, that's perfect."

Me:
"Agent M."

Agent M:
"Yes, sir."

Me:
"Contact Pixar."

I paused.

Me:
"Oh, right."

Agent M:
"...Yes?"

Me:
"Take the sleep-paralysis ghost with him."

Agent M:
"...Why?"

Me:
"He can't do all the dubbing alone."

A Few Years Later

Pixar Animation Studio – Dubbing Room

Director:
"Fantastic! That monster voice is perfect!"

Jangsanbeom:
"...Thank you."

Ghost:
"Shall I call the next character name?"

A Few Months Later

Agent M:
"General... we have a situation."

Me:
"What is it this time?"

Agent M:
"We received a call from Pixar.
Jangsanbeom has requested leave."

Me:
"Why?"

Agent M:
"He says he has too much work."

Me:
"What kind of work?"

Agent M:
"Two Pixar animations, three game dubbing projects,
and monster voices for films..."

A brief silence.

Me:
"...Have him take medical leave for voice protection,
and send him on vacation to Yosemite near Hollywood.
He's getting paid well anyway, right???"

Agent M:

"Yes, sir."

Me:
"What about the sleep-paralysis ghost?"

Agent M:
"He's recording commercials."

Me:
"Tell him to take a break after that too.
And recommend quince tea—good for the throat."

And so, the two voice actors became indispensable figures in Hollywood,
and the legend says they are still thriving there to this day.

He doesn't mimic voices.
He replaces them.

chapters.title: Case 6 - Dugeoksini
chapters.content:
One morning, Agent M came to work grumbling.

Agent M:
"General... Dugeoksini caused trouble again."

Me:
"What did he do this time?"

Agent M:
"He frightened people walking at night, sir.
They panicked while running away and got injured."

Me:
"Dugeoksini."

Dugeoksini:
"...Yes."

Me:
"Why do you keep scaring people and driving them into terror?"

Dugeoksini:
"I... feed on human fear."

Me:
"So fear is basically your food?"

Dugeoksini:
"...Yes. Something like that."

Me:
"Can you operate during the day?"

Dugeoksini:
"...Yes."

Me:
"Then wouldn't it be more fun to mess with bad guys instead?"

Dugeoksini:
"...That sounds amazing.
Scamming the scammers sounds like a blast, right?
And messing with bad guys is way more fun, isn't it?"

Me:
"How about joining the police special forces—psychological operations?
Plenty of bad guys there.
You get to work, become a hero...
and you get paid."

Dugeoksini:
"...I'd be grateful, sir.
When do I start?"

Me:
"Agent M! Submit a recommendation to the National Police Agency!
And if that doesn't work, send one to the U.S. CTU (Counter Terrorist Unit).
I think you'd work perfectly with Jack Bauer."

Agent M:
"...Yes, sir. I'll submit it right away."

And so, it is said that Dugeoksini went on to workbetween Korea and the United States,
serving as a psychological warfare specialist against terrorists,

and contributing to world peace.

chapters.title: Case 7 - No Minor Ghost
chapters.content:
Case 7 – No Minor Ghost

And so, the formidable ghosts of Korea each began new lives,
and we no longer had any problems.

We held an autumn sports festival.

As they took part in relay races, tug-of-war, and the like,
their hands would naturally brush, their bodies would collide.


After the games, at the after-party, they shared food and drinks,

and through these natural encounters, connections formed.

Bachelor ghosts, maiden ghosts, egg ghosts, restroom ghosts—
all kinds of spirits shared their hardships and stories with one another.

Many of them became couples,
and as a result, their han—their lingering resentment—gradually dissolved,
leaving them with no reason to remain in this world.

They went to the afterlife, received judgment,
and after a period of correction and rehabilitation, were reborn.

However, there was one request even the GCA could not resolve.

We politely declined Samshin Grandmother's request
to be married off.

Because she is not a ghost—
she is a deity.

After that, protests from the gods poured in,
and it is said that we are now preparing to establish
DCA – Deity Consultant Agency.
